title: Above the Clouds
brief: Original concert overture for symphony orchestra and organ, about 4 min 20 s, C major: a misterioso intro, an Allegro, the big tune in G, a storm in C minor, a still interlude for solo violin and cello, and the big tune fff in C with the organ, then a coda.

sections.intent: Intro: open fifths over a low C; a distant horn, a clarinet in the minor and a flute share the head of the theme.
Departure: spiccato strings in 3+3+2; the horns state the Allegro theme, then the orchestra repeats it ff.
Turn: the head passes down through the woodwinds as the music slows into G major.
Open sky: the big tune in the first violins over harp, cellos and a horn in countermelody; C minor darkens it.
Storm: the Allegro theme in C minor, the head in stretto, a chromatic climb to G7(b9), a stroke and silence.
Stillness: a solo violin sings the big tune in Ab, a solo cello answers in imitation; Db leads to G7.
Ascent: over a G pedal an inner line climbs D-Eb-E-F; Ab and Bb break into C.
Above the clouds: the whole big tune fff in C with countermelody, chorale, bells and organ.
Coda: the head in stretto through the brass, Ab-Bb-C, F minor once more, a held C major chord.

decisions: One head (G-C-D, then E) opens the horn call, the Allegro theme, the big tune, the storm theme and the coda: thematic transformation, so the big tune sounds familiar when it finally arrives whole.

The big tune is held back: the open sky plays its first ten bars and turns to C minor where it should climb; only the last section plays all sixteen, with its summit, two rising sixths and the F minor (iv) under it.

Moments planned for the listener: a 4-3 suspension and a deceptive cadence inside the tune, the stretto, the stroke and 2.5 s of silence, a new solo voice after it, the Neapolitan, and the deceptive turn from G7 to Ab before the last section.

Balance after Rimsky-Korsakov: trumpets and trombones -19 to -21 dBFS, horns -20 to -23, the melody strings -19 to -21, woodwinds -24. Soft solos (horn, clarinet, flute, violin, cello) have tracks of their own, levelled apart from the tutti.

Expression: dynamic layers crossfaded along each sustained part's dynamics, crossfaded legato on single lines, the distant horn slurred, every part at its stage depth with one hall send, loudness range 12 LU.
Deliberate tensions: passing tones in the themes (the head's D over C), the clarinet's D (#11) over Ab, the G7(b9) of the storm, the A-Ab line over F and F minor.
